issue.title: M0: Real fn Dictations recorded notInserted (typedSince) though they paste
issue.body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0 (bug)
**Test seam:** live app + headless (the late-text guard)
**Modules:** LexiconCore, KeyInput, AppText

## What happened

Live checks, 2026-10-11: real fn Dictations are recorded `notInserted` with reason `typedSince` **even though the text pastes**. 3 of 3 on heads that carry main after ba6d600 (#57 @ 6bd8bf3, #68 @ 3cb91a6). Test-hook WAV Dictations on the same builds come out `inserted`. On #56's own earlier heads (0d3adf5, bf7c0b9) real fn Dictations were inserted (47 of 48). Jake's daily app is installed at ba6d600, so it may be affected.

Suspect: the typedSince watcher counts an event caused by the fn key itself (its flagsChanged on release) or Lexicon's own Cmd-V, introduced around #56's final merge (787b841, folding #71's Lexicon into LexiconSystem) or the shared InputClock.

## What to build

Find the cause (bisect between bf7c0b9 and ba6d600 if needed) and fix it so Lexicon's own fn release and its own paste never count as "typed since". Keep the guard working for real keys and clicks from Jake. The History status must match what happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A headless test reproduces it (fn release and Lexicon's own Cmd-V events through the real watcher) and fails before the fix.
- [ ] Live checks: 10 real fn Dictations into a scratch field, all `inserted`; a real key typed between fn-up and paste still gives `notInserted`/`typedSince`.
- [ ] State whether the daily build ba6d600 has the bug.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

issue.title: Retro: Live checks queue, sittings, Dev data and bench
issue.body:
## Parent

#88 (M0 retro). Every box below is one accepted retro change; its full write-up (problem, verified evidence, change, expected effect) is in "Change details" at the bottom.

**Milestone:** retro, before M1 (wave 1)
**Size:** L.
**Files this ticket owns (no other retro ticket touches them):** `scripts/live-lane.sh`, `scripts/live-request.sh` (new), `scripts/dev-run.sh`, `scripts/lib/fn-listeners.sh`, `scripts/import-lexicon.sh`, `scripts/install-model.sh`, `scripts/lag-report.sh`, `scripts/bench.sh` (new), `scripts/test-live/` (new), `scripts/checks/32-live-scripts-tests.sh` (new).
**Needs the Live checks session for:** - agent: a dry run of one queued request with two hands-off items on main; bench.sh on History open; the fake-listener refusal.
- Jake: none (the mock sitting has zero physical steps).

## What to build

Live requests as typed issue comments in one queue, hands-off items that run alone, scheduled sittings with a preflight, fn checks that refuse while another listener runs, safe moves of Dev's data, and a bench that records its load.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **1. The queue.**
  - `scripts/live-request.sh` posts `Live checks request: <branch> @ <sha7>` with typed items: kind, gesture, target, speak, cue, observable, pass bar and needs. It refuses unpushed or dirty trees and missing fields, naming the field.
  - `live-lane.sh queue` lists requests in arrival order.
  - Hands-off items run once HID idle time shows Jake isn't typing (verify the ioreg reading first).
  - Long waits become background timers that release the lane.
  - Prove: refuses with an unpushed commit, and with an item missing its observable. #53's hold-fn step can't render without its speak field.
- [ ] **1. Sittings and preflight.**
  - `live-lane.sh sitting render` produces one numbered checklist with total minutes, and prerequisites as their own steps.
  - `sitting start` writes the marker on Jake's go. Default sitting slots are 11 AM and 6 PM Pacific, moved freely; a sitting is scheduled only when physical items exist (Jake prefers hands-free: anything a hook or headless run can check never becomes a Jake item).
  - Acks are by step number.
  - The preflight refuses: another fn listener; a hook item on a release bundle; an item whose needed feature has no use site at the head; an item the issue marks out of scope. It prints the exact open command.
  - Prove: refuses #64's item 8 at 113f5cc with "nothing reads doubleTapWindow at this sha", refuses a hook item on a release bundle, and refuses with a fake fn listener running, naming the process.
- [ ] **30. fn listeners.**
  - `require_no_fn_listeners` in fn-listeners.sh refuses for fn-dependent callers, and also matches a second Dev copy. dev-run.sh uses it.
  - Result headers record "fn listeners: none".
  - `live-lane.sh daily quit|reopen` (Q8: yes): lane holder only, no Dictation in progress, quits from the menu, reopens `~/Applications/Lexicon.app`.
  - Prove: with a fake listener process, dev-run.sh's fn path refuses with the message, and WAV-hook checks still run.
- [ ] **41. Dev data.**
  - `import-lexicon.sh dev` writes to scratch unless `--dev-data` is passed, which runs `live-lane.sh check`.
  - `install-model.sh dev` runs the same lane check.
  - `live-lane.sh park` and `restore`: keep the models link, use a manifest, restore on exit, refuse foreign folders.
  - Prove: a dev import with no flag writes nothing under Lexicon Dev; park then restore leaves models as a link with an equal file count.
- [ ] **42.** The sitting marker the guard reads (see `sitting start`).
- [ ] **13. Bench.**
  - `scripts/bench.sh <budget>`: interleaved runs, at least 5 per side; the exclusion rule fixed first; a 0.5 s load sampler plus power state; a provisional label measured against background load; refusals of single runs and of a final verdict while another fn listener runs.
  - lag-report.sh reads the sampler file.
  - Prove: refuses one run per side. On History open (hands-off), it prints p50, p95, the load minimum, median and maximum, and PASS or PROVISIONAL.
- [ ] Tests in `scripts/test-live/`, run by `scripts/checks/32-live-scripts-tests.sh`.

Each box is done only when its "Prove" step passes on a real past case, as written. A check you add must fail on the named past mistake before your fix makes it pass.

## Blocked by

none.

pr.body:
Refs #157

## Summary

Live checks gets one typed queue on the issues, sittings only when Jake has physical items, fn checks that refuse instead of warn, safe moves of Dev's data, and a bench that records its load. Scripts only; no app code changes.

```text
builder:      scripts/live-request.sh post <issue> <items>   "Live checks request: <branch> @ <sha7>"
                typed items: kind, gesture, target, speak, fn, cue, observable, pass, needs (+ minutes for Jake)
                refuses a dirty or unpushed head, and any item missing a typed field (named)
Live checks:  scripts/live-lane.sh
  queue                     open requests oldest first (newest per issue, until a "Live checks:" result), due timers first
  idle [s]                  HID idle time (ns from IOHIDSystem): hands-off items run once Jake isn't typing
  timer <s> <label>         a long wait (memory settle, an eval) becomes a timer and frees the lane,
                            unless Dev's data is parked or a sitting is open
  preflight <issue>         refuses: another fn listener (fn items), a hook item on a release bundle,
                            a bundle at another or dirty commit, a needed Swift name with no use site,
                            a needed #N still open, an item the issue marks out of scope; prints the open command
  sitting render|start|ack|end   one numbered checklist, prerequisites first, total minutes, next 11 AM / 6 PM
                            Pacific slot; start writes live-sitting.open (the marker #154's guard reads); acks by step
  daily quit|reopen         lane holder only, real login HOME only, no Dictation in progress,
                            Quit from its own menu (never a kill), reopen ~/Applications/Lexicon.app
  park | restore            Dev's data aside with a manifest; models link and lane files stay; restore on release/take;
                            refuses a folder park didn't make
scripts/lib/fn-listeners.sh require_no_fn_listeners (by executable path; daily, other Lexicon/Dev copies, prototypes)
scripts/dev-run.sh          refuses on a listener; --no-fn for WAV-hook and Accessibility-only runs
scripts/import-lexicon.sh   dev -> scratch under TMPDIR; --dev-data runs the lane check
scripts/install-model.sh    dev runs the lane check
scripts/bench.sh            history-open | launch, A/B interleaved, >= 5 runs per side, 0.5 s load sampler + power,
                            PROVISIONAL over 1.5x the measured background load or while a listener runs
scripts/lag-report.sh       --load <sampler file>
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new tests against `main`'s scripts: dev-run's fn path runs with the daily Lexicon up (#141), a plain dev import writes into Lexicon Dev (#71), install-model dev runs without the lane. 8 FAIL.
  **After:** `scripts/checks/32-live-scripts-tests.sh`: 99 ok, 0 FAIL (request 18, lane 58, scripts 23), in a fake HOME with fake gh, ps, lsappinfo, osascript and open.
- `scripts/check.sh` green at efd2ab4: 454 tests, import check, scorer, eval with no worse scores.
- Prove steps, as tests:
  - #53's hold step without `speak`: `item 1 (Hold): no speak field`, both from `items` and from `sitting render`.
  - an item missing its observable, and an unpushed commit: refused, nothing posted.
  - #64's item 8 at the real 113f5cc: `nothing reads doubleTapWindow at this sha (113f5cc)`.
  - a hook item on a release bundle; a compiled fake listener: `Lexicon Indicator is running (pid N, <path>)`.
  - dev-run with a fake daily listener refuses with the message; `--no-fn` still runs.
  - park then restore: models still a link, same file count; a stray file and an interrupted park still restore.
  - real case: `import-lexicon.sh dev` on a synthetic file imported 2 Terms and 1 Rule into scratch; the real Lexicon Dev folder was unchanged.
  - bench refuses 1 run per side; a run at #64's load (26 to 46) is PROVISIONAL.
- HID idle verified on this Mac: nanoseconds, grows about 2 s per 2 s sample, resets on input.
- Live checks: requested (dry run of the queued request on #157, bench.sh on History open, the fake-listener refusal, park/restore on Dev's real data). Its `Live checks:` comment on #157 is the evidence.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Scripts only. `dev-run.sh` now refuses while the daily Lexicon runs; WAV-hook runs need `--no-fn`. Every request item now needs an `fn: yes|no` field.

During self-review a Haiku verifier ran `daily quit` under a fake HOME and quit Jake's real daily Lexicon from its menu. Fixed here: `daily` refuses unless HOME is the login home, and the tests stub lsappinfo, osascript and open. `import-lexicon.sh dev` no longer writes into Dev unless `--dev-data`. The workflow.md, live-checks skill and implement-ticket text for the queue land with #162, #161 and #158; until then the scripts' headers are the reference. The checks/32 step runs once #153's check.sh runs `scripts/checks/*.sh`.

**Blast Radius:** live-checks

## Install

Code only.

Check: nothing in the app; Live checks' next sitting comes from `scripts/live-lane.sh sitting render`.

comments.body: Reviewer: held for a file overlap. #169 (#153) also edits `scripts/import-lexicon.sh` and `scripts/install-model.sh`, and it was Ready first. `git merge-tree` shows a content conflict in `import-lexicon.sh`. Once #169 merges, merge `origin/main` here and keep #169's `$SWIFT_FLAGS` form, since `swift-flags.sh` no longer sets `"$@"`. Then post Ready.

**Reviewer verdict: don't merge yet** (head 27c6dc0). Three fixes, all small.

One critic reviewed this, and a verifier reproduced the data finding on a fake HOME. I read `daily()` and the queue's comment parsing myself. The main merge with #169 keeps `$SWIFT_FLAGS`.

**What holds:**
- **`daily` acts only on the real Mac and the real app, and never kills.** It checks that HOME is the real login home, that the running process is `~/Applications/Lexicon.app`, and that no Dictation is in progress, then quits from the app's own menu.
- **park and restore never reach the daily folder.**
- **`idle` reads only HIDIdleTime.**
- **The fn-listener check** counts `Lexicon.app.old` and doesn't match the harness or Dev.
- **No shell injection from comments.** Comment text reaches only printf, awk, jq and quoted git args.
- **bench** alternates the two sides with at least 5 runs each.
- **Scripts and tests.** `sh -n` passes, and the tests use a fake HOME.

**Before merge:**
1. **The queue trusts anyone's comments.** The repo is **public**, and `live-lane.sh` (`queue`, `request_body`, `issue_text`, ~lines 105-135) reads every comment with no author check. So a stranger's "Live checks request:" becomes a typed item the Live checks agent runs on the real Mac (fn, Accessibility, paste). A stranger's "Live checks: <head>" can also mark a real request done. Keep only comments whose `author.login` is the repo owner (`jparker2006`, which every session posts as), and add a test with a foreign author.
2. **`daily quit` needs only the lane, not an open sitting** (`live-lane.sh:364-397`). Any session that takes a free lane can quit Jake's daily copy outside a sitting. The guard can't see inside the script, so #167 doesn't stop it. Jake's Q8 was "quits and reopens the daily app around a sitting". Require `live-sitting.open` for `daily quit`, and for `reopen` too, or have `reopen` require that a `quit` from this sitting happened.
3. **Restore can move Dev's real History into a temp folder (verified).** `restore` (`:435-455`) first moves every non-kept file in `Lexicon Dev` into a temp folder, then puts back the manifest's entries. After an interrupted restore, the retry moves the already-restored `History.sqlite` into `$TMPDIR/lexicon-dev-unparked.*` and still prints "restored". A park killed after its first manifest line does the same on the next automatic `take`. Treat manifest entries already in Dev as restored, move aside only what the manifest doesn't name, and make `restore` check the folder against the manifest before it says "restored".

**Worth fixing (medium):**
- **Ctrl-C leaves processes running.** `bench.sh` and `test-live/lib.sh` set only an EXIT trap, which `/bin/sh` doesn't run on SIGINT, so Ctrl-C leaves the load sampler, or a fake listener in tests, running. Add `trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP`. A fake `Lexicon.app` from this suite (pid 9965, ppid 1, its test folder gone) is still running on the Mac now, and it will make real fn runs refuse. Whoever started it should stop it by that pid.
- **A crash leaves the sitting marker behind.** `live-sitting.open` has no liveness check or expiry, so after a crashed sitting, Dev permission resets stay allowed until someone runs `sitting end`. Record the holder's pid in it and treat a dead pid as closed.
- **bench under another fn listener.** It gives a PROVISIONAL verdict where #157 item 13 asks for a refusal, and `scripts.test.sh:65` pins that. Jake's call: refuse, or keep PROVISIONAL.
- **One bad request breaks rendering.** A single open request without `fn:` makes `sitting render` exit 1 for every issue.

**Later:**
- **"In progress" ends at fn-up,** not at the outcome line.
- **Two interrupts that leave a mess** (nothing is lost):
  - a park killed before its manifest leaves a folder that both park and restore refuse;
  - `take` exits 1 still holding the lane if its restore dies.
- **The menu-click Quit** probably needs an Automation grant for System Events, which the Install section doesn't mention.
Fixed review at f7b4d2d.

**Reviewer verdict: merge with notes** (head 5ef22b1, f7b4d2d plus main with #170). All three fixes are read and correct:
- **Owner-only comments.** The queue, `request_body` and `issue_text` keep only the repo owner's comments.
- **Daily quit and reopen.** `daily quit` needs an open sitting, which `sitting_open` checks by the holder pid and its start time, clearing a dead session's marker. `daily reopen` only reopens a copy `daily quit` closed, and `sitting end` reopens it.
- **Restore.** It keeps entries that are already back and checks that every manifest entry is in Dev before it removes the manifest; `set -eu` makes that check stop the script.
- **Ctrl-C.** `bench` and the test lib exit on INT, TERM and HUP.

Live checks passed items 1 to 4 at efd2ab4. CI is green.

**Later:**
- A `## ` heading on a `Live checks:` line keeps a request queued, with no warning. Match after stripping leading `#` and spaces, or warn.
- `bench.sh` prints "Terminated: 15" job noise when it stops its sampler.
- `history-open` on a History without older days ends on the harness's FAIL line, with no A or B lines and no verdict.
- The bench verdict judges A's absolute p95 alone, so identical code got FAIL at 104 ms against B's 98 ms. Judge the budget against B too, or call a gap within noise a tie.
- Jake's call: a bench under another fn listener says PROVISIONAL with no final verdict; #157 item 13 asked for a refusal. Recommend refusing.

issue.title: M0: First-run setup and start at login
issue.body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0  
**User stories:** 92, 93, 94, 95  
**Test seam:** live app  
**Modules:** LexiconUI, LexiconCore, LocalParakeet (install)

## What to build

A small setup window on first run: (1) Microphone, the macOS prompt; (2) Accessibility, opens the right System Settings page, polls trust and relaunches as soon as it's granted; (3) download the speech model (about 609 MB, with progress; the spec lists this as an assumption Jake can veto); (4) "Hold fn and say something", text lands in that window. It also checks the globe key setting. Only Microphone and Accessibility are requested.

- Start at login via `SMAppService.mainApp`, on by default, registered on first run, with a toggle in the menu bar menu.
- A missing or revoked permission shows a warning dot on the menu bar icon; clicking it reopens that step. No popups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fresh data folder, setup takes Jake from nothing to a working Dictation without leaving the window except for System Settings.
- [ ] Granting Accessibility relaunches the app automatically.
- [ ] After a reboot, Lexicon is running and fn works.
- [ ] Revoking Microphone shows the warning dot; clicking it reopens that step.

## Blocked by

- #56

comments.body: Building: taking this (Claude)

Live checks: claude/issue-57 @ 6bd8bf3

issue.title: M0: First-run setup and start at login
issue.body:
## Parent

#36 (Spec: Lexicon v0)

**Milestone:** M0  
**User stories:** 92, 93, 94, 95  
**Test seam:** live app  
**Modules:** LexiconUI, LexiconCore, LocalParakeet (install)

## What to build

A small setup window on first run: (1) Microphone, the macOS prompt; (2) Accessibility, opens the right System Settings page, polls trust and relaunches as soon as it's granted; (3) download the speech model (about 609 MB, with progress; the spec lists this as an assumption Jake can veto); (4) "Hold fn and say something", text lands in that window. It also checks the globe key setting. Only Microphone and Accessibility are requested.

- Start at login via `SMAppService.mainApp`, on by default, registered on first run, with a toggle in the menu bar menu.
- A missing or revoked permission shows a warning dot on the menu bar icon; clicking it reopens that step. No popups.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a fresh data folder, setup takes Jake from nothing to a working Dictation without leaving the window except for System Settings.
- [ ] Granting Accessibility relaunches the app automatically.
- [ ] After a reboot, Lexicon is running and fn works.
- [ ] Revoking Microphone shows the warning dot; clicking it reopens that step.

## Blocked by

- #56
